name: Local Test for an Ample One-Concept Extension
statement:
Let $S\subseteq Q_F$ be nonempty and ample, let $a
otin S$, and let $I=\{f:a^{\{f\}}\in S\}$. Then $S\cup\{a\}$ is ample exactly when $I
otin\operatorname{Sh}(S)$, equivalently when the extension is isometric, or when $\operatorname{Diff}(a,x)\cap I
e\varnothing$ for every $x\in S$. The punctured $I$-cube around $a$ is automatically present in $S$. When the conditions hold, $a$ is a corner with unique maximal-cube support $I$, $\operatorname{Sh}(S\cup\{a\})=\operatorname{Sh}(S)\mathbin{\dot\cup}\{I\}$, and $I$ is a minimal nonface of $\operatorname{Sh}(S)$.
proof: Restrict $S$ to the face agreeing with $a$ outside $I$. Its cube complement is ample and connected, contains $a$, and contains none of its neighbors, so it is the singleton $\{a\}$; hence all other vertices of the $I$-face lie in $S$. The missing-support condition is therefore exactly the condition that every $x\in S$ has a shortest path from $a$ beginning with an $I$-edge. If the extension is ample, deleting $a$ between two ample classes makes $a$ a corner and removes exactly the shattered support $I$. Conversely the punctured cube strongly shatters $I$, so the Sandwich inequality and $|S|=|\operatorname{Sh}(S)|$ force equality for the extension. Parallel faces through neighbors of $a$ show that every proper subset of $I$ was already shattered.
